summary: SPACE MISSION: BEYOND EARTH is a full-cycle 3D space mission simulator developed by the OrbitShift team using the Unity engine (C#) for the "Space Mission Design Game" challenge. In academic curricula, orbital mechanics and onboard systems are typically studied in isolation, making it difficult for students to visualize how, for instance, the addition of a single scientific instrument increases payload mass, drains batteries, and depletes energy reserves. Our simulator integrates spacecraft design, launch, and flight operations into a single interactive model. Players assemble a spacecraft from eight categories of subsystems, navigate 11 stages of orbital insertion across 10 scenarios set throughout the solar system, and manage six key parameters in real time—based on NASA’s International Space Station (ISS) ECLSS standards—throughout the entire duration of the mission in a single-player mode.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

SPACE MISSION: BEYOND EARTH guides players through the four core stages of a real NASA mission:

1. Hangar & Architecture Design: Players choose from 10 Solar System mission scenarios (including Low Earth Orbit, Lunar reconnaissance, Mars transit, and outer-planet flybys) and assemble a spacecraft across 8 modular hardware categories while balancing strict payload mass, electrical power, data memory, and budget constraints.

2. Launch & Orbital Insertion: An 11-stage launch and trajectory verification module checks thrust-to-weight ratios, delta-v margins, and orbital parameters inspired by NASA's General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT).

3. In-Flight Operations & ECLSS Survival (180-Day Simulation): During cruise (with 1x, 2x, and 4x time compression), players monitor 6 real-time telemetry bars (0–100%) calibrated to NASA baselines: Solar Power (1,361 W/m² LEO irradiance), Oxygen (1.14 kg/day per crewmember with tank mass), Water (4.99 kg/day closed-loop baseline), Nutrition (2,975 kcal/day), Hull Integrity, and Crew Morale. Players switch subsystem power across 4 modes (Off 0%, Eco 15%, Normal 35%, Overdrive 70%) and respond to dynamic in-flight anomalies every 15–25 mission days.

4. Mission Debrief: A post-flight engineering audit evaluates survival margins, science return, and system resilience.

CREATIVE FEATURES & TEAM ROLES

Players can fly as 1-role Mission Control crew modeled on NASA mission segments: Navigator (Flight Dynamics & Burns), Flight Engineer (Avionics & Power Bus), ECLSS Officer (Life Support & Recycling), and Mission Commander (Communications & Crisis Triage).

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

The simulator closes the educational gap between textbook physics and systems engineering for high school and university STEM students, demonstrating cascading subsystem trade-offs without requiring specialized engineering software.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

- Engine & Programming: Unity 2022.3 LTS (3D Engine), C# (procedural HUD, telemetry plots, orbital physics, and idempotent scene setup via SpaceMissionProjectSetup.cs and MarsMissionGame.cs).

- Use of Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: Google Gemini (LLM) was used to assist with C# script prototyping, structuring technical documentation, and translating presentation materials (EN/RU/KZ). All visual assets in the presentation use authentic archival NASA photography with zero AI-generated NASA logos or insignia.
